cells.quote: Online H5P interactive case study activities were introduced for the first time in 22/23 and we observed a 30% engagement rate with these activities. In comparison, a 65% completion rate of weekly formative (“practise”) MCQ questions (available on Moodle) was observed, indicating we can do more to sign post students to these interactive activities.
cells.note: Descriptive Moodle activity-completion percentages; no test statistic or effect size was reported.

O.outcome_detail: student ratings of engagement, learning support and enjoyment

result.effect: 25% increase in positive case-study tutorial ratings in 22/23 versus 20/21

cells.quote: Feedback to all questions was improved in the 21/22 cohort vs. the 20/21 cohort and maintained (or further improved) in the 22/23 cohort (Figure 3) to “overall positive” from “neutral positive,” with fewer students rating activities negatively. Changes implemented in the 21/22 and 22/23 academic years to the case study focussed tutorials, led to none of the students surveyed rating the tutorials as negative compared with the 20/21 academic year (Figure 3B) with a 25% increase in positive ratings in 22/23 vs. 20/21.
cells.note: Cohort-year comparison; students were not randomly assigned, and no test statistic or inferential effect estimate was reported.

D.treatment: updated case-study-focused PBL unit delivery in 22/23

cells.quote: We observed an increase in student engagement with the case study tutorial sessions, with attendance increasing by 20% for the academic year 22/23 compared with 21/22.
cells.note: Attendance was compared across academic years using selected tutorial sessions; no random assignment, test statistic, or uncertainty estimate was reported.

D.treatment: bespoke interactive H5P practical-support activities in 22/23
D.comparison: bespoke interactive H5P practical-support activities in 21/22

O.outcome_detail: proportion of students completing the online practical-support package

cells.quote: A 5% increase in students completing the online practical support package was observed from the 21/22 to 22/23 academic years, although we observed overall low engagement with this activity (<20%) which is not unexpected as the in-person laboratory practical classes were very well attended.
cells.note: The study reports Moodle activity-completion proportions across cohorts; no test statistic or effect size is printed.

D.treatment: Blood Science unit with in-person PBL case-study activities
D.comparison: other Biomedical Sciences units with the same student cohort

cells.quote: In further support of our strategy to incorporate PBL activities within our unit design, comparison of student feedback for the Blood Science unit compared with other Biomedical Sciences units with the same student cohort in 22/23, demonstrates a substantially higher rate in positive feedback for the Blood Science unit (+30%).
cells.note: Same-cohort unit comparison; the study does not report random assignment, a statistical test, or a printed standardized effect size.
